gen_risks.description: Electricity tariffs set below the cost of service cause persistent financial deficits across sector utilities, threatening the ongoing operational and financial viability of energy infrastructure.
gen_risks.mitigation: Utilize analytical support and technical assistance under the project to assist the government in formulating and implementing a comprehensive tariff reform strategy and utility financial sustainability plan.
gen_risks.evidence: The current electricity price is below the cost of service causing financial difficulties for sector utilities.

gen_risks.description: Administrative and technical capacity constraints within the implementing entity could lead to implementation delays and contract management inefficiencies.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish a dedicated Project Management Office (PMO) under the Ministry of Energy, engage an Owner's Engineer to support procurement and supervision, and provide targeted capacity-building programs.
gen_risks.evidence: Previous infrastructure projects in Mongolia have experienced implementation delays due to the administrative and technical capacity constraints of the implementing agencies.

gen_risks.description: An aging, rigid coal-fired Combined Heat and Power (CHP) generation fleet limits system flexibility and restricts the dispatch and grid integration of Variable Renewable Energy (VRE).
gen_risks.mitigation: Reinforce the 220kV transmission backbone to expand transfer capacity and conduct technical assistance studies on grid planning and VRE integration strategies.
gen_risks.evidence: Most of the CHP units are aging... inefficient and highly polluting. The CHP plants make the power system inflexible, making it indispatchable...

gen_risks.description: Overhead high-voltage transmission line construction and operation pose bird collision and habitat disruption risks along sensitive ecological zones and wetlands.
gen_risks.mitigation: Realign the transmission line corridor away from sensitive wetlands, install flight diverters and bird-friendly tower solutions, and execute a comprehensive Bird Management Plan.
gen_risks.evidence: Transmission lines in Mongolia often involve bird collision and other biodiversity issues

gen_risks.description: Extreme winter conditions, severe cold, high wind loads, and climate hazards could cause structural damage to transmission infrastructure and disrupt project construction.
gen_risks.mitigation: Apply climate-resilient design and engineering standards for transmission towers and insulators to withstand extreme wind loading, freezing temperatures, and natural hazards.
gen_risks.evidence: Mongolia is prone to risks from climate hazards such as flooding, wildfires, and landslides, with exposure to drought and extreme cold...

gen_risks.description: High reliance on imported construction materials (75-80%) exposes the project to supply chain disruptions, border delays, and material cost volatility.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct early supply market intelligence, perform advance procurement planning, and incorporate rated criteria evaluating material sourcing and delivery strategies.
gen_risks.evidence: The construction sector in Mongolia has been heavily reliant on imports, with statistics showing that 75-80% of construction materials are sourced from outside...

gen_risks.description: The short construction season in Mongolia risks civil works overruns into winter, causing project completion delays of up to an entire year.
gen_risks.mitigation: Initiate advance procurement to ensure contracts are awarded prior to the start of the construction season, and evaluate contractors on their technical plans for seasonal optimization.
gen_risks.evidence: the seasonal nature of civil works in Mongolia adds more risks... If it cannot be completed before winter, the Project will have more delays

gen_risks.description: Substandard or unqualified local construction materials could compromise structural integrity and safety standards of transmission infrastructure.
gen_risks.mitigation: Incorporate non-price rated evaluation criteria assessing material quality control strategies, and enforce mandatory quality testing supervised by the Owner's Engineer.
gen_risks.evidence: 40% of construction materials were found unqualified in the local market.

gen_risks.description: Civil works along the right-of-way may cause temporary disruption to local herders' pasture access, water wells, and community safety.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement the Stakeholder Engagement Plan (SEP), Resettlement Policy Framework (RPF), and operate a accessible two-stage project Grievance Redress Mechanism (GRM).
gen_risks.evidence: temporary social risks and impacts... temporary restriction of access to resources by local herders (for example, pasture, wells, etc.)

gen_risks.description: Frequent turnover of decision-making officials and high-level political interference in procurement decisions may cause significant procedural delays.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish clear procurement workflows and delegation of authority in the Project Operational Manual, maintain oversight through the Project Steering Committee, and enforce World Bank review procedures.
gen_risks.evidence: Frequent change of the decision-making officials for the Project. Interference of the high-level officials in procurement decision making which leads to delays.

gen_risks.description: Evaluation Committee members' lack of familiarity with World Bank procurement regulations and English bidding documentation could prolong contract evaluations.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide structured training on World Bank procurement regulations, evaluation procedures, and standard bidding documents for PMO staff and Evaluation Committee members prior to procurement launching.
gen_risks.evidence: Evaluation Committee members normally do not have knowledge and experience in procurement for Bank-financed projects...

gen_risks.description: Complex Treasury Single Account flow-of-funds procedures involving local currency investment sub-accounts could create disbursement bottlenecks and vendor payment delays.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish a segregated USD Designated Account with commercial zero-balance pass-through mechanisms and defined payment approval workflows in the Financial Management Manual.
gen_risks.evidence: Delays and bottlenecks in the project funds flow arrangements that got complicated with the addition of an investment project account within the Treasury...

gen_risks.description: Gender-based biases and structural obstacles in the power sector limit female representation and career progression in engineering and management roles.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct a comprehensive gender gap assessment, introduce gender-responsive HR practices, provide targeted professional development, and monitor workforce gender target metrics.
gen_risks.evidence: gender-based biases may be an obstacle to women’s employment and especially to career progression at NPTG.

gen_risks.description: Lack of grid redundancy in single-circuit transmission corridors leads to severe prolonged power supply outages during line faults.
gen_risks.mitigation: Construct a second 220kV double-circuit transmission line between Baganuur and Choir substations to establish full double-circuit redundancy.
gen_risks.evidence: The region served by the existing Baganuur-Choir single circuit line experienced a supply outage of 33 hours in 2021 caused by a fault on the line.

gen_risks.description: Delays in establishing the Project Management Office and finalizing operational documentation could postpone project effectiveness and early implementation.
gen_risks.mitigation: Set the adoption of the Project Operational Manual and formal establishment of the PMO as legal conditions of loan effectiveness.
gen_risks.evidence: PMO is not yet in place and no financial management staff has been appointed

gen_risks.description: Occupational health and safety hazards during construction and maintenance including high-voltage exposure, work at height, and electromagnetic fields.
gen_risks.mitigation: Enforce Labor Management Procedures (LMP), align safety protocols with World Bank Environmental, Health, and Safety Guidelines, and require full-time contractor OHS specialists.
gen_risks.evidence: occupational health and safety (OHS) risks associated with live power lines, working at height, electric and magnetic fields (EMF).

gt_risks.description: Political and governance risks are rated Substantial. The parliamentary election was held in June 2024 and a new coalition government was formed, with representation of all three major political parties. While there may be risks of disagreement on the approval of individual projects, these risks will be mitigated by the strong alignment of the proposed operation with the NRP and the new Government Action Plan for 2024-2028.
gt_risks.mitigation: Continued engagement with key stakeholders, including government and the parliament, through ongoing analytical and technical support on VRE integration and energy sector reform, will help mitigate risks going forward. The Development Partner Group, co-chaired by the World Bank and UNDP, will also offer a donor coordination platform to maintain political momentum for RE integration.

gt_risks.description: The macroeconomic risk is rated Substantial. Mongolia's economic outlook is dependent on global macroeconomic factors, in particular commodity prices. Despite recent positive short-term developments from coal and agricultural exports, Mongolia still needs to strengthen fiscal and external buffers to respond to future shocks and continue reforms aimed at diversifying the economy.
gt_risks.mitigation: To mitigate these risks and manage external balances, the World Bank has been, and will continue to be, supporting the authorities in restoring fiscal and external buffers through analytical and advisory work.

gt_risks.description: The sector strategies and policies risk is rated Substantial. Substantial risk still exists due to institutional fragmentation, lack of policies to promote RE projects, and lack of clear commitment of reforms, especially related to tariff reforms that are crucial to make the sector viable and be able to refinance projects.
gt_risks.mitigation: Mitigation measures include actively engaging in multi-stakeholder coordination meetings and providing technical advice and capacity building to key stakeholders.

gt_risks.description: The institutional capacity for implementation and sustainability risk is rated Substantial. The implementing agency MOE and NPTG have experience implementing World Bank-funded projects; however, there is a substantial risk that newly hired PMO staff may not have sufficient capacity, which could potentially lead to implementation delays.
gt_risks.mitigation: The PMO will be strengthened with experienced consultants and targeted training and capacity building. Mitigating measures include the World Bank's scrutiny of PMO members' selection, including a review of the TOR and providing no objection to the qualification criteria of the staff.

gt_risks.description: Fiduciary risk is rated Substantial. There are substantial risks due to the reliance of MOE on a newly constituted PMO, which may cause delays in processing payments, conducting IFRs, and other reporting requirements; the construction sector in Mongolia is often subject to delays and cost overruns. Potential procurement risks include (i) likelihood of time and cost overruns due to weak contract management capacity, and (ii) significant procurement delays due to delayed initiation of procurement and establishment of needed staffing arrangements.
gt_risks.mitigation: Capacity building through customized training and TA is a central element of the Project, along with strong project supervision and contract management capacity building; MOE will continue to directly provide intensive support to the PMO. Procurement risks are mitigated by (a) establishing a PMO with appropriate procurement and technical staff per FIDIC contract standards; (b) clearly defined workflow in decision-making within the MOE/PMO procurement manual; and (c) extensive market engagement to stimulate market participation.
